title: real-world-100-repo-sweep-2026-05-09
workingTreeNote: dirty working tree during sweep; no source edits were made by this run

dependencyPrep.notes: No dependency-prep commands were required or run for this sweep; validation executed directly against cloned repositories.

findings: Validated 100 repositories; 53 had issues, 21 included parsing failures, and 21 had failed files.
Coverage gaps were common: 8 repositories had zero discovered files and 21 had >=70% skipped files.
Several repositories produced very high repeated validation issue counts (e.g., 100s to 1000s), increasing triage noise.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Add robust parser/error classification for known non-standard or templated files to reduce hard failed-file counts and confusing parse output.
productRecommendations.rationale: 21/100 repos had parsing failures and 21/100 had failed files; this blocked developer interpretation in a large slice of the corpus.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Improve skipped-coverage reporting with explicit per-repo reason aggregation and a concise coverage confidence signal.
productRecommendations.rationale: 8 repos had zero discovered files and 21 repos had >=70% skipped files, often leaving unclear what DollarLint actually checked.

productRecommendations.recommendation: Provide grouped/compacted issue summaries by schema/file/root cause alongside full details.
productRecommendations.rationale: Some repos generated large volumes of repetitive findings (for example >100 to thousands), making next actions harder to identify quickly.

productDecisions: No source changes were made in this sweep run; recommendations are recorded for follow-up prioritization.
followUp: Run a targeted second 100-repo sweep biased toward actively maintained application/server repositories (fewer docs-only projects) to reduce zero-discovery noise.
Prototype parser classification and skipped-coverage summarization improvements, then rerun a representative 20-repo subset for before/after UX comparison.
Prioritize triage of high-volume outliers (ui, netdata, zed, opencode, immich) to distinguish true repo invalidity from reportability noise.
